one_liner: Supervisory Navy role leading acquisition strategy, plans, and DoD 5000 documentation for the Conventional Prompt Strike hypersonic weapons program office.
fit_summary: This role requires at least one year of GS-13-equivalent experience applying DoD 5000 acquisition management to Major Defense Acquisition Programs, plus supervisory acquisition expertise. Nothing on file shows defense acquisition experience; IEM consulting and policy knowledge are relevant to emergency management, not weapons-system acquisition. Unless your IEM work involved DoD acquisition documentation, you are unlikely to qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public, but this is a flyer for anticipated vacancies; applications go through the separate 'How to Apply' instructions, not this posting.
Specialized experience: one year at NH-03/GS-13 level using Navy/DoD acquisition principles (DoD 5000) to plan and manage documents for Major Defense Acquisition Programs.
Security clearance: Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access required.
Program Management Series 0340 qualification standards apply; resume limited to 2 pages.
strategy: Before investing time, honestly check whether any IEM work involved DoD acquisition documents, MDAP support, or federal contract/budget analysis; if not, skip this posting.
If you have relevant experience, state it explicitly with DoD 5000 terms, dates, hours per week, and GS-13-level complexity in a two-page resume.
Frame IEM client work around planning, stakeholder coordination, and leadership briefings only where accurate, and never inflate; the posting warns inflated qualifications lead to disqualification.
Follow the flyer's 'How to Apply' directions exactly, since applications are not accepted through the flyer itself, and act between Oct 28 and Nov 10, 2026.

Better targets: FEMA (Reservist/CORE, GS-0089 emergency management), Virginia VDEM, Prince William County or Fairfax OEM, and congressional or state legislative staff roles that use your policy and people skills.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] [program/acquisition] efforts at IEM, developing [strategy/plan documents] for [review/milestone], [hours]/week, [dates].
Briefed [client leadership level] on [contract, budget, or requirements] implications for [program], coordinating [number] internal and external stakeholders.
Led/supervised [number] staff producing [deliverables] on [timeline], ensuring compliance with [federal regulation/framework].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you developed an acquisition strategy for a program under DoD 5000.
How would you prepare leadership for a milestone acquisition review with budget shortfalls?
Describe how you have supervised a team producing time-sensitive documents for external stakeholders.
How do you resolve conflicts between program requirements and contract or budget constraints?
watch_outs: Requires specific DoD 5000/MDAP acquisition experience your background does not show.
SCI clearance required; obtaining it takes time and eligibility is not guaranteed.
Notice-of-vacancy flyer only; there may be no actual hires and no result letters.
Supervisory NH-4 senior role; little room to grow into qualifications on the job.
